headline: Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman told staff its new in-house base model beats the one behind OpenAI's GPT-5.6 while using a quarter of the computing power.
score_reason: A startling comparative claim, but it is Microsoft's own, untested publicly, and based on private tests.
importance_line: It matters for the Microsoft-OpenAI partnership and the cost of training AI, but outsiders cannot yet check the claim and OpenAI has not responded.
summary: Business Insider reports that Mustafa Suleyman, chief executive of Microsoft AI, told employees at a town hall on Thursday that Microsoft's new base model, MAI-Base-2, is stronger than the pre-trained model behind OpenAI's GPT-5.6 and used one quarter of the computing power, based on technical information Microsoft has about OpenAI's models. Microsoft is a major investor in and partner of OpenAI, which did not respond to a request for comment; Suleyman also claimed 12 times less computation than DeepSeek used for a comparable model.
notes: Full text read. Claims are Microsoft's own; Microsoft declined further comment.
